question: The rule that ‘it can move only one square in any direction’ applies to whom in a game of chess?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The King**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The King can move exactly one square horizontally, vertically, or diagonally. This rule is what makes the King's movements unique in chess.
 
• Unlike other pieces, such as the Queen or the Rook, the King has a limitation in its range of movement, emphasizing the need for protection.
 
• The King is also involved in a special move called castling, which is the only move that allows two pieces, the King and a Rook, to move at the same time.
 
• Protecting the King is the primary objective in chess, as the game ends when the King is checkmated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chess is believed to have originated in India around the 6th century AD, known as Chaturanga back then.
 
• It spread into Persia, became known as Shatranj, and later evolved in Europe where it got its current form in the 15th century.
 
• The International Chess Federation (FIDE), founded in 1924, governs international chess competition.
 
• Magnus Carlsen of Norway is one of the highest-rated chess Grandmasters as of the current records.
